competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sentence asks for problems solved, and the body of the node does exactly that in one step. Combination at seed 42, 'A book is 21 cm long. A spoon is 12 cm long. If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?', and difference at seed 46, 'A book is 19 cm long. A pencil is 10 cm long. How many cm longer is a book than a pencil?'. Every item in this node is answerable from the information rendered in the stem; none depends on a picture, a ruler image or an unstated quantity, and each states both operands and the unit wanted.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both nouns the sentence names are covered separately. Length carries the majority, e.g. seed 50, 'A notebook is 20 cm long. A spoon is 16 cm long. How many cm longer is a notebook than a spoon?', and seed 501, 'A notebook is 30 cm long. A shoe is 29 cm long. If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?'. Distance is present in its own right at seed 603, 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 3 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 9 m. Which distance is longer?', and at seed 601, 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the school and the market: centimeters or meters?'. Both the combining and the comparing shapes of problem are found.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Fifteen of the sixteen items are one-step sums or differences with totals no larger than 59, as at seed 501, 'A notebook is 30 cm long. A shoe is 29 cm long. If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?'. Seed 604, 'Convert 4 m to cm.', is the outlier: arriving at 400 requires the metre to centimetre relation applied four times, that is a multiplication by 100 that a Grade 2 Quarter 2 learner has not been taught, and it is the only item in the node making that demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three problem shapes appear across three formatters, with the operands and objects varied rather than recycled. End-to-end combination at seed 44, 'A ruler is 15 cm long. A spoon is 12 cm long. If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?'; how-much-longer difference at seed 55, 'A spoon is 12 cm long. A crayon is 6 cm long. How many cm longer is a spoon than a crayon?'; and distance reasoning at seed 605, 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 3 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 10 m. Which distance is longer?'. Object pairings change seed to seed and distractors sit one or two units from the key.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 604, 'Convert 4 m to cm.', is not a problem involving length and distance; it is a bare unit conversion, and converting between metres and centimetres is a later grade competency, so a Grade 2 Quarter 2 node reaches past its own sentence by carrying it. The remainder stays in scope, although seed 602, 'Which is longer: 13 cm or 6 cm?', is a bare magnitude comparison that solves no problem and would sit more naturally in the measure-and-compare node than in this one.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every noun takes a fitting unit at a believable size. Seed 55, 'A spoon is 12 cm long. A crayon is 6 cm long. How many cm longer is a spoon than a crayon?', and seed 500, 'A pencil is 20 cm long. A ruler is 30 cm long. If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?', keep hand-held objects in cm within ruler range. Distance goes to metres and stays there: seed 601, 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the school and the market: centimeters or meters?', answers m, and seeds 603 and 605 state the bench, gate and tree distances in m, so no item in the node contradicts the unit rule that seed 601 teaches.
